subject: Dedicated capacity smoothing — annual invoicing and term discount structures

Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity proposal & ramp structure

Hi Anya —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great to see the live latency profile on your high-throughput workloads. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture a starting commercial structure for dedicated capacity that aligns with Vanguard AI's seasonal usage and stickiness goals.

High-level idea (please treat as starting point):
- 3-year committed term, annual invoicing with prepay option per year.
- Year 1: 50 dedicated GPUs (steady-state smoothing allowed)
- Year 2: increase to 150 GPUs
- Year 3: 300 GPUs
- We can offer a blended committed rate that improves as you move up the ramp; additional burst capacity billed at an overage rate.

Questions we had for you:
1) Do you need the ability to true-up mid-year (monthly or quarterly) vs. only at year boundaries?
2) Is Vanguard able to do an annual prepay for each contract year, or do you prefer a multi-year single prepay?
3) Any constraints from procurement on early-termination liabilities or capital vs. operating treatment?

I've attached a brief term sheet that lists our standard annual prepay discounts and an initial SLA proposal (redwood_pricing_term_sheet_v1.pdf). If it helps, I can loop in Marcus and Karthik for a short call to go through discount scenarios and smoothing options.

Would you be available for a 30-min sync next week?

Best,

Kimberly —

Thanks for the write-up and the terms. Vanguard is interested but we have a few constraints to flag from procurement before we lock into a prepay structure:

- Preference for annual prepay (per year) rather than a large multi-year prepayment; we typically treat multi-year prepay as capital approval, which slows procurement.
- We need smoothing / flexibility: we can commit to a target number of GPUs per year but would like a monthly true-up window (30–60 days) to avoid overpaying during seasonal dips.
- Early termination: procurement will want a cap on liability or a pro-rata refund mechanism if we need to downsize due to business reasons.

Could you send scenarios that show: 1) annual prepay with 12-month true-up; 2) annual prepay + small credit bank for burst months; and 3) a hybrid where Year 1 is more conservative with an escalation clause?

I've attached a doc with our ramp questions (vanguard_ramp_questions.docx). Happy to jump on a call with the pricing team.

Thanks,

Scenarios requested by the customer:
A) Annual prepay at beginning of each year with 12-month lookback true-up (monthly usage true-up allowed within 60 days)
B) Annual prepay + small per-year credit bucket for burst months (example: 5% of committed capacity available as burst)
C) Conservative Year 1 (smaller prepay) with escalation clauses in Years 2–3 if volume targets are met (true-up annually)

Please include recommended term discounts (if any) and any suggested SLA credit ramps.

Thanks — can we get preliminary numbers by Tue EOD?

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Vanguard ramp questions — pricing scenarios (analysis attached)

Team —

I ran a quick model and attached the spreadsheet (pricing_model_vanguard.xlsx). High level options with blunt ranges below (numbers are illustrative — final model in the sheet):

Option 1 — 3-yr single prepay (aggressive):
- Effective discount: 18–24% off list depending on front-loaded prepay.
- Pros: lowest unit $/GPU-month. Cons: procurement friction for multi-year single prepay; higher breakage exposure.

Option 2 — Annual prepay (recommended baseline):
- Yearly prepay with ascending committed volumes; 8–14% discount year-over-year as you ratchet capacity (we can provide a 14% discount in Year 3 based on commitment).
- Include 30–60 day monthly true-up (customer keeps first 5% cushion without penalty).
- Early-termination: pro-rata refund less 6 months of committed payments (we can soften this in SOW).

Option 3 — Hybrid phased prepay (low Year1, true-up + earn-back credits):
- Year1 prepay smaller (e.g., 25% of target) with option to elect an earned discount once Year1 usage >= 90% of target.
- Overages priced at a modest premium (15–20% over committed rate).

Some implementation notes:
- We should offer a transparent invoice schedule and a simple true-up calculation so procurement can model GAAP/CapEx treatment.
- For smoothing, offering a 5% burst buffer and a 60-day true-up window tends to be acceptable to mid-market procurement teams.

Attaching the sheet with per-GPU-month numbers and example invoice schedules.

—Karthik

Subject: Proposal: annual prepay structure (Option 2) — Vanguard AI

Anya / Procurement —

Thanks for the detailed feedback and the ramp questions. Based on Karthik's models, we recommend Option 2 (annual prepay with annual ratchet and 30–60 day monthly true-up) as the lowest-friction path that balances your procurement preferences with unit economics.

Key commercial summary (sample numbers):
- Year 1: prepay for 50 GPUs at $X,XXX per GPU/month effective (after 9% Year 1 discount) — invoice on 2026-07-01 for Year 1.
- Year 2: prepay for 150 GPUs at a stepped effective rate (12% discount) with true-up window through March of Year 2.
- Year 3: prepay for 300 GPUs with 14% discount (ratchet if usage thresholds are hit earlier).
- Burst buffer: 5% monthly buffer allowed; overages billed monthly at +15% to committed rate.
- Early termination: pro-rata refund less 6 months of committed payments (we are open to capping this to ease procurement concerns).

I attached a proposed SOW and sample invoice schedule for your legal & finance teams (vanguard_proposed_SOW_v1.pdf). For transparency, here's our internal deal link if you want to track: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345

If that structure works, can you confirm the preferred billing cadence (annual prepay by PO, or net-30 invoiced annually) and whether Vanguard requires any additional accounting language about capital treatment?

I can do a 30-min call Thursday to finalize redlines — what time works for you?

Best,
Marcus Lin

Marcus / Kimberly —

Appreciate the clarity and the sample SOW. Vanguard is prepared to move forward with Option 2 (annual prepay + 30–60 day monthly true-up) with one small set of asks before legal drafts redlines:

1) Please formalize a 60-day true-up in the SOW (customer request) with a clean formula for the calculation.
2) Add an additional 2% commercial credit (applied to Year 1 invoice) if Vanguard and Redwood agree to run a channel integration pilot (joint GTM) within the first 12 months.

If you can include the above and send a redline-ready SOW, procurement will circulate for final approval. We prefer annual prepay via PO with net-30 payment terms.

Looking forward to closing this—happy to hop on a short call if you prefer to finalize verbally.
